name: Exchange Online — Transport (Mail Flow) Rule Created or Modified
description:
Attacker objective
Intercept, redirect, copy or silently drop organisational email by creating or modifying an Exchange transport (mail-flow) rule.

Attack logic
Transport rules act on all mail flow. An attacker can add a rule that blind-copies mail to an external address, redirects specific messages, or deletes security-related notifications to hide activity.

Why this detection works
The unified audit log records transport-rule create/modify/remove operations with the acting principal; these are infrequent administrative changes.

False positives
A legitimate mail-administration change to routing, disclaimers or compliance rules.

Tuning
Correlate with change control; review the rule's actions (bcc/redirect/delete) and conditions; allowlist sanctioned mail-admin automation.

Required telemetry
o365.audit RecordType 1, Operations 'New-TransportRule' / 'Set-TransportRule' / 'Remove-TransportRule' (Parameters, user.name=actor).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. Review the transport rule's conditions and actions (especially blind-copy, redirect or delete).
2. Confirm the change was authorised; a rule that exfiltrates or drops mail is high-risk — revert and investigate the actor.
false_positives: A legitimate mail-administration change to routing, disclaimers or compliance rules.
